extracted.intended_audience: Sierra Club members and environmental advocates preparing public comments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for members and advocates on drafting effective public comments to agencies or officials on environmental issues, emphasizing tone, length, personalization, and use of chapter resources. Focuses on persuasive messaging and coordinated advocacy actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization over templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized letters are more effective than utilizing pre-written templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer writing an individualized comment rather than submitting an unmodified template; if using a template, personalize it to reflect your own experience or perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity / recommended length
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep your comments brief; one page or shorter recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit comments to about one page to respect reviewers' time and increase the likelihood your points are read; be concise and prioritize the most important points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity and local impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific and explain how the issue affects you and, if possible, how it impacts your community and/or state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, personal, and local examples of harm or benefit (e.g., health, economic, cultural impacts) to make the comment more persuasive to decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise and direct messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Be concise and direct (e.g., "100% renewable energy will keep our air and water clean").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short, clear declarative statements and avoid jargon; lead with a simple, memorable message that communicates the core ask or fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values-based framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Connect to widely held values identified in your community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame arguments in terms of shared community values (e.g., health, safety, clean air/water, economic opportunity) to broaden appeal beyond technical audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make messages compelling and meaningful
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft language that resonates emotionally and substantively—use storytelling, vivid examples, or clear stakes to make the comment memorable and impactful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage advocacy resources and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Use grassroots lobbying days, public comment workshops (some chapters provide slide decks), calls to Members of Congress, coordinated comment letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in chapter-organized activities, attend workshops to improve comment quality, use provided slide decks or templates as starting points, and consider coordinated letters or calls to amplify impact.
